claims.statement: For the exact ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star family and every actual lower-half eligible p with x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, 2p<=alpha, if W[p+1]C[p-1]<=W[p]C[p] for W=sum_i r_i A_i, then the actual strict current-p selectors include a tip and selected MASS A=sum_i r_i e_i T_i[p-2]>=b delta D_j. Here x is the actual first strict descent, coefficients are integer zero-extended, j=p-2, delta=q-j, b=e0+sum_i r_i e_i, and original tag multiplicities are retained. No weighted-deck instance or arbitrary-tree extension is proved.
claims.scope: Conditional universal implication for m>=1 and r_i in {2,3,4}, retaining the actual first strict descent, all three eligibility guards, current-p strict selectors, original tip multiplicities r_i, endpoint multiplicity one, and integer zero extension.
claims.reason: The guards make the added binomial summand strictly rise at x; log-concavity then gives C[p]/C[p-1]<1. Positive support gives W[p]>0, so the assumed weighted comparison forces Delta_p W<0 and an active tip. Since its original multiplicity B is at least 2, the established 3/2 branchwise bound pays b=B+e0. The weighted-deck premise remains open.

claims.statement: On the exact contract's actual eligible lower-half rows, the accepted relative margin implies S<=bD_j-(1-t+t/delta)A. Consequently exact-ratio payment implies S<=0, and selected MASS A>=b delta D_j implies that payment.
claims.scope: Only the exact path-star selected aggregate at actual eligible lower-half p, retaining the actual first strict descent, all three guards, current-p strict selectors, integer zero extension, and original multiplicities. No converse or arbitrary-tree conclusion.
claims.reason: Division by positive delta*C[j] preserves the accepted margin's direction and yields Delta_j T_i<=-kappa*T_i[j]. Summing with nonnegative original weights proves the aggregate upper bound. Since kappa*delta=1+(delta-1)(1-t)>=1, MASS implies payment. The aggregate bound cannot be reversed.

limitations: The weighted-tip-deck comparison itself is not proved; the first claim is conditional on that open premise.
No full-family census, path-star counterexample, Lean verification, or arbitrary-tree residual-aggregate bridge was produced.
Finite exact scalar checks audit inequality direction and boundary arithmetic only; they are not universal evidence.
